Here is the full MSBuild review for this solution:

---

# MSBuild Project File Review — `StyleIssues.sln`

## Summary

| File | Issues |
|------|--------|
| `Directory.Build.props` | 2 |
| `Directory.Build.targets` | 1 |
| `LibA/LibA.csproj` | 5 |
| `LibB/LibB.csproj` | 2 |
| `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` | 1 |
| `fsharp/Directory.Build.props` / `.targets` | 0 (OK) |
| `fsharp/OrderService/OrderService.fsproj` | 0 (OK) |

---

## 🔴 Errors (likely broken or causing silent misbehavior)

### 1. `Directory.Build.props` — TargetFramework condition is dead code (AP-21)

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation for single-targeting projects. The SDK sets `TargetFramework` from `TargetFrameworks` during target execution — long after `.props` files are evaluated. This condition will **never** be true, so documentation files are never generated.

**Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets`:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Property defaults set in `.targets` override project-level values

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` files are imported **after** the project file. Because MSBuild uses last-write-wins semantics, these unconditional assignments override anything the project file sets. `LibB` tries to set `TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` but it silently has no effect.

**Fix:** Move these to `Directory.Build.props` as conditional defaults:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

This allows individual projects to override if needed.

---

### 3. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
  <DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** This **replaces** the entire `DefineConstants` value, destroying the SDK-provided `TRACE` and `DEBUG` constants. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop working.

**Fix:** Append instead of overwrite:
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 4. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Unquoted condition value

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** The property expansion and comparison value are both unquoted. If `$(Configuration)` is empty or contains spaces, this produces an MSBuild evaluation error or always-false result.

**Fix:** Quote both sides:
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 5. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` — Incorrect F# file compilation order

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** F# is order-sensitive — files listed first can only reference types defined in files listed before them. `Services.fs` is listed before `Domain.fs`, meaning Services cannot use Domain types (but likely needs to), and Domain cannot use anything from Services. The correctly-ordered `OrderService.fsproj` has `Domain.fs` first. This will likely cause `FS0039` (undefined value/type) errors.

**Fix:** Reorder to dependency order:
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

---

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns that should be fixed)

### 6. `Directory.Build.props` — Analyzer package leaks to consumers

```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```

**Problem:** Analyzer packages should use `PrivateAssets="all"` to prevent them from becoming transitive dependencies of any NuGet package produced from these projects. Without it, consumers of your package will also get StyleCop enforced on *their* code.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

---

### 7. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Legacy `<Reference>` with HintPath to packages folder

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

**Problem:** This is a `packages.config`-style reference in an SDK-style project. It bypasses NuGet restore, won't get transitive dependency resolution, and the `net6.0` asset is wrong for a `net8.0` project. The hardcoded path also breaks on any machine without that exact folder.

**Fix:** Replace with a proper PackageReference:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 8. `LibA/LibA.csproj` & `LibB/LibB.csproj` — Hardcoded absolute `OutputPath`

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```

**Problem:** Absolute Windows paths break on Linux/macOS, break for any developer who doesn't have a `C:\builds` directory, and prevent parallel builds for different configurations (Debug vs Release go to the same folder).

**Fix:** Remove these entirely (use SDK defaults `bin\$(Configuration)\$(TargetFramework)\`) or use relative paths with configuration:
```xml
<OutputPath>$(MSBuildProjectDirectory)\..\artifacts\$(MSBuildProjectName)\$(Configuration)\</OutputPath>
```

---

### 9. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Redundant `Include` + `Update` in same ItemGroup

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

**Problem:** The SDK already auto-includes all `*.cs` files. The explicit `Include` creates a **duplicate** item (CS2002 warning). The `Update` should stand alone to modify metadata on the already-globbed item.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` and keep only the `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

### 10. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Custom target without Inputs/Outputs (breaks incrementality)

```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** Without `Inputs` and `Outputs` attributes, this target runs on **every** build, even when nothing has changed. This defeats incremental build optimization. Additionally, the version is hardcoded rather than derived from a property.

**Fix:**
```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build"
        Inputs="$(MSBuildProjectFile)"
        Outputs="$(IntermediateOutputPath)PrintVersion.marker">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version $(Version)" />
  <Touch Files="$(IntermediateOutputPath)PrintVersion.marker" AlwaysCreate="true" />
</Target>
```

---

## 🔵 Suggestions (improvements for maintainability)

### 11. No Central Package Management (CPM)

The solution references packages in multiple places (`Directory.Build.props` for StyleCop, `LibA.csproj` for Newtonsoft.Json) without a `Directory.Packages.props`. As the solution grows, version drift becomes likely.

**Suggestion:** Create `Directory.Packages.props` with `<ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>` and centralize all `Version` attributes there.

---

### 12. `fsharp/` sub-tree uses empty `.props`/`.targets` to block parent inheritance

This is a valid technique, but the empty files could use `<Import>` with `GetPathOfFileAbove` to selectively pull in *some* parent settings (e.g., `Company`, `Copyright`) while blocking C#-specific ones.

---

## 🟢 Positive (good practices observed)

- **F# `OrderService.fsproj`** has correct file ordering (`Domain` → `Services` → `Program`).
- **`fsharp/Directory.Build.props`** correctly short-circuits parent `.props` to prevent C#-specific analyzer leakage into F# projects — well-documented with a comment.
- **Use of SDK-style projects** throughout (no legacy `<Import Project="$(MSBuildToolsPath)...">`).
- **Solution-level build infrastructure** (`Directory.Build.props`/`.targets`) is in place, showing intentional build organization.

---

## Priority Remediation Order

| Priority | Issue | Impact |
|----------|-------|--------|
| 1 | Move defaults from `.targets` → `.props` (#2) | LibB override silently broken |
| 2 | Fix `DefineConstants` overwrite (#3) | `DEBUG`/`TRACE` constants lost |
| 3 | Move TFM condition to `.targets` (#1) | Doc generation never activates |
| 4 | Fix unquoted condition (#4) | Potential eval error |
| 5 | Fix F# file order (#5) | Compilation failure |
| 6 | Replace legacy Reference (#7) | Wrong TFM asset, restore bypass |
| 7 | Remove hardcoded paths (#8) | Cross-platform breakage |
| 8 | Add `PrivateAssets` to analyzer (#6) | Leaks to consumers |
| 9 | Fix duplicate Compile item (#9) | CS2002 warning |
| 10 | Add Inputs/Outputs to target (#10) | Slower incremental builds |

## 🔴 Errors (likely broken or causing silent misbehavior)

### 1. `Directory.Build.props` — TargetFramework condition is dead code (AP-21)

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation for single-targeting projects. The SDK sets `TargetFramework` from `TargetFrameworks` during target execution — long after `.props` files are evaluated. This condition will **never** be true, so documentation files are never generated.

**Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets`:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Property defaults set in `.targets` override project-level values

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` files are imported **after** the project file. Because MSBuild uses last-write-wins semantics, these unconditional assignments override anything the project file sets. `LibB` tries to set `TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` but it silently has no effect.

**Fix:** Move these to `Directory.Build.props` as conditional defaults:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

This allows individual projects to override if needed.

---

### 3. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
  <DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** This **replaces** the entire `DefineConstants` value, destroying the SDK-provided `TRACE` and `DEBUG` constants. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop working.

**Fix:** Append instead of overwrite:
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 4. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Unquoted condition value

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** The property expansion and comparison value are both unquoted. If `$(Configuration)` is empty or contains spaces, this produces an MSBuild evaluation error or always-false result.

**Fix:** Quote both sides:
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 5. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` — Incorrect F# file compilation order

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** F# is order-sensitive — files listed first can only reference types defined in files listed before them. `Services.fs` is listed before `Domain.fs`, meaning Services cannot use Domain types (but likely needs to), and Domain cannot use anything from Services. The correctly-ordered `OrderService.fsproj` has `Domain.fs` first. This will likely cause `FS0039` (undefined value/type) errors.

**Fix:** Reorder to dependency order:
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

---

### 6. `Directory.Build.props` — Analyzer package leaks to consumers

```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```

**Problem:** Analyzer packages should use `PrivateAssets="all"` to prevent them from becoming transitive dependencies of any NuGet package produced from these projects. Without it, consumers of your package will also get StyleCop enforced on *their* code.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">

</Reference>
```

**Problem:** This is a `packages.config`-style reference in an SDK-style project. It bypasses NuGet restore, won't get transitive dependency resolution, and the `net6.0` asset is wrong for a `net8.0` project. The hardcoded path also breaks on any machine without that exact folder.

**Fix:** Replace with a proper PackageReference:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 8. `LibA/LibA.csproj` & `LibB/LibB.csproj` — Hardcoded absolute `OutputPath`

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```

**Problem:** Absolute Windows paths break on Linux/macOS, break for any developer who doesn't have a `C:\builds` directory, and prevent parallel builds for different configurations (Debug vs Release go to the same folder).

**Fix:** Remove these entirely (use SDK defaults `bin\$(Configuration)\$(TargetFramework)\`) or use relative paths with configuration:
```xml
<OutputPath>$(MSBuildProjectDirectory)\..\artifacts\$(MSBuildProjectName)\$(Configuration)\</OutputPath>
```

---

### 9. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Redundant `Include` + `Update` in same ItemGroup

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

**Problem:** The SDK already auto-includes all `*.cs` files. The explicit `Include` creates a **duplicate** item (CS2002 warning). The `Update` should stand alone to modify metadata on the already-globbed item.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` and keep only the `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

### 10. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Custom target without Inputs/Outputs (breaks incrementality)

```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** Without `Inputs` and `Outputs` attributes, this target runs on **every** build, even when nothing has changed. This defeats incremental build optimization. Additionally, the version is hardcoded rather than derived from a property.

**Fix:**

<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build"
        Inputs="$(MSBuildProjectFile)"

  <Exec Command="echo Building version $(Version)" />
  <Touch Files="$(IntermediateOutputPath)PrintVersion.marker" AlwaysCreate="true" />

<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation for single-targeting projects. The SDK sets `TargetFramework` from `TargetFrameworks` during target execution — long after `.props` files are evaluated. This condition will **never** be true, so documentation files are never generated.

**Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets`:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Property defaults set in `.targets` override project-level values

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` files are imported **after** the project file. Because MSBuild uses last-write-wins semantics, these unconditional assignments override anything the project file sets. `LibB` tries to set `TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` but it silently has no effect.

**Fix:** Move these to `Directory.Build.props` as conditional defaults:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

This allows individual projects to override if needed.

---

### 3. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
  <DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** This **replaces** the entire `DefineConstants` value, destroying the SDK-provided `TRACE` and `DEBUG` constants. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop working.

**Fix:** Append instead of overwrite:
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 4. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Unquoted condition value

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** The property expansion and comparison value are both unquoted. If `$(Configuration)` is empty or contains spaces, this produces an MSBuild evaluation error or always-false result.

**Fix:** Quote both sides:
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 5. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` — Incorrect F# file compilation order

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** F# is order-sensitive — files listed first can only reference types defined in files listed before them. `Services.fs` is listed before `Domain.fs`, meaning Services cannot use Domain types (but likely needs to), and Domain cannot use anything from Services. The correctly-ordered `OrderService.fsproj` has `Domain.fs` first. This will likely cause `FS0039` (undefined value/type) errors.

**Fix:** Reorder to dependency order:
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

---

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns that should be fixed)

### 6. `Directory.Build.props` — Analyzer package leaks to consumers

```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```

**Problem:** Analyzer packages should use `PrivateAssets="all"` to prevent them from becoming transitive dependencies of any NuGet package produced from these projects. Without it, consumers of your package will also get StyleCop enforced on *their* code.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

---

### 7. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Legacy `<Reference>` with HintPath to packages folder

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

**Problem:** This is a `packages.config`-style reference in an SDK-style project. It bypasses NuGet restore, won't get transitive dependency resolution, and the `net6.0` asset is wrong for a `net8.0` project. The hardcoded path also breaks on any machine without that exact folder.

**Fix:** Replace with a proper PackageReference:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 8. `LibA/LibA.csproj` & `LibB/LibB.csproj` — Hardcoded absolute `OutputPath`

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```

**Problem:** Absolute Windows paths break on Linux/macOS, break for any developer who doesn't have a `C:\builds` directory, and prevent parallel builds for different configurations (Debug vs Release go to the same folder).

**Fix:** Remove these entirely (use SDK defaults `bin\$(Configuration)\$(TargetFramework)\`) or use relative paths with configuration:
```xml
<OutputPath>$(MSBuildProjectDirectory)\..\artifacts\$(MSBuildProjectName)\$(Configuration)\</OutputPath>
```

---

### 9. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Redundant `Include` + `Update` in same ItemGroup

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

**Problem:** The SDK already auto-includes all `*.cs` files. The explicit `Include` creates a **duplicate** item (CS2002 warning). The `Update` should stand alone to modify metadata on the already-globbed item.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` and keep only the `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

### 10. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Custom target without Inputs/Outputs (breaks incrementality)

```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** Without `Inputs` and `Outputs` attributes, this target runs on **every** build, even when nothing has changed. This defeats incremental build optimization. Additionally, the version is hardcoded rather than derived from a property.

**Fix:**
```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build"
        Inputs="$(MSBuildProjectFile)"
        Outputs="$(IntermediateOutputPath)PrintVersion.marker">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version $(Version)" />
  <Touch Files="$(IntermediateOutputPath)PrintVersion.marker" AlwaysCreate="true" />
</Target>
```

---

## 🔵 Suggestions (improvements for maintainability)

### 11. No Central Package Management (CPM)

The solution references packages in multiple places (`Directory.Build.props` for StyleCop, `LibA.csproj` for Newtonsoft.Json) without a `Directory.Packages.props`. As the solution grows, version drift becomes likely.

**Suggestion:** Create `Directory.Packages.props` with `<ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>` and centralize all `Version` attributes there.

---

### 12. `fsharp/` sub-tree uses empty `.props`/`.targets` to block parent inheritance

This is a valid technique, but the empty files could use `<Import>` with `GetPathOfFileAbove` to selectively pull in *some* parent settings (e.g., `Company`, `Copyright`) while blocking C#-specific ones.
